answering.asked_for: the production preflight mapping observation and refusal, plus deterministic engine fixtures

I_WIRED_IT_AND_IT_IS_NOT_A_FIXTURE_PROBL.what_I_did: put the call in `single_worker.worker_preflight`, exactly where I and the review have said it belongs, and ran tests.tools.test_single_worker
I_WIRED_IT_AND_IT_IS_NOT_A_FIXTURE_PROBL.what_happened: the suite HUNG and had to be killed. The traceback shows the probe reaching `observe_runtime_identity` through `EnginePort(effective_engine_run(engine_run))` -- and `effective_engine_run(None)` is `_engine_run`, which is `subprocess.run` on the real argv (single_worker.py:563). So a preflight that does not inject an engine attempts a REAL `docker run`.
I_WIRED_IT_AND_IT_IS_NOT_A_FIXTURE_PROBL.why_that_is_not_a_fixture_inconvenience: it is a hazard in the placement itself. `worker_preflight` is reached with `engine_run=None` by callers that are not starting anything -- `operations_from` composes it, and the composed judgment workers do the same -- and its engine DEFAULTS to the live subprocess runner. Putting a live engine round-trip there means any composition attempts to start a container. That is true of production as much as of the fixtures.
I_WIRED_IT_AND_IT_IS_NOT_A_FIXTURE_PROBL.reverted_and_verified: the wiring is out, the comment naming the exact line is back, and the six affected suites are green. I checked afterwards for real side effects: `docker ps -a --filter name=baton-identity` names nothing and no `.identity-probe-*` directory remains anywhere under /var/tmp.
I_WIRED_IT_AND_IT_IS_NOT_A_FIXTURE_PROBL.this_supersedes_my_earlier_reason: I said twice that the blocker was the fixtures. The fixtures are a consequence; the cause is that the probe is a live engine round-trip in a function whose engine defaults to the live runner.

the_design_that_follows.shape: the mapping becomes a DEPLOYMENT-RECORDED fact, exactly as the workspace group already is: `configure_identity_mapping(store, identity, observed_identity)` records a proved observation with the journal-and-projection cross-check `configured_workspace_group` uses, and `configured_identity_mapping(store)` mints it back.
the_design_that_follows.then_preflight_only_READS: it requires the record and refuses when it is absent or names another identity -- an early, enforced refusal before any Job execution effect, with NO engine round-trip in preflight at all.
the_design_that_follows.who_takes_the_observation: the deployment, once, through `oci.observe_runtime_identity` -- the helper this Work has now had accepted -- at the same point it provisions the workspace group. A real engine is used where a real engine is already being used.
the_design_that_follows.what_it_costs_the_fixtures: one recorded fact in the shared setUps that already call `configure_workspace_group`, rather than teaching dozens of ad-hoc `class Engine:` stand-ins to model a container run.
the_design_that_follows.why_this_is_mine_to_decide: FINDING.md leaves the supported engine mapping to the implementer; this is a placement, not a new owner question.
